settlement-survey-s1.title: Three ways of dividing farmland, seen from above

image.alt: Three numbered panels drawn from above. Panel 1: odd-shaped fields whose edges follow a winding stream, a tree and a rock. Panel 2: a grid of equal squares with straight roads at right angles and a few farmhouses. Panel 3: narrow strips of land side by side, each running back from a river, with a house at the river end of each strip.
image.caption: A LevlPrep drawing of three survey methods.

settlement-survey-s2.title: The Land Ordinance of 1785, in summary
settlement-survey-s2.text: In 1785 the US Congress (then under the Articles of Confederation) passed the Land Ordinance. In our summary: land west of the Appalachian Mountains was to be surveyed before it was sold. Surveyors drew east-west and north-south lines to divide it into townships, squares 6 miles on each side. Each township was split into 36 sections of 1 square mile (640 acres). One section in each township was set aside to support a public school. Land was then sold by the section or in parts of sections.

items.q: Which panel shows the township and range system?
options: Panel 2
Panel 1
Panel 3
Panels 1 and 3 together

why.correct: Township and range divides land into a grid of squares, so fields and roads meet at right angles.
options: Right: panel 2 is a grid of equal squares with straight roads, the mark of township and range.
Panel 1 has odd-shaped fields that follow a stream and markers such as a tree and a rock: metes and bounds.
Panel 3 has long, narrow strips running back from a river: long lots.
Neither panel 1 nor panel 3 is a grid: look for the equal squares.

items.q: Which panel most likely shows farmland along the St. Lawrence River in Quebec, Canada, first divided by French settlers?
options: Panel 1
Panel 2
Panel 3
Panels 1 and 2 equally

why.correct: The long lot system gave each family a narrow frontage on the river, the main road of the time, and a long strip running inland.
options: Panel 1 shows metes and bounds, used in colonies such as Virginia, not in French Quebec.
Panel 2 shows the US township and range grid.
Right: French settlers divided land into long lots, each with a narrow river front.
Neither has the long, narrow strips running from a river that French settlement left.

items.q: Why did the method in panel 3 give each farm a narrow strip instead of a square?
options: So that the farms would match the squares of a grid
So that fields could follow the shapes of trees and rocks
So that roads could cross the farms at right angles to each other
So each farm could reach the river for water and travel

why.correct: Long lots gave every farm a share of the most valuable thing nearby, river access, which is also why the houses line up along the river.
options: Equal squares are the goal of township and range, panel 2.
Following natural features is metes and bounds, panel 1.
Roads at right angles mark the grid in panel 2.
Right: the river was the highway and water source, so each lot was cut to give every family a piece of riverbank.

items.q: Panel 1 shows boundaries that follow a stream and use a tree and a rock as corners. In which part of the United States is this method most common?
options: The Midwest and West, in states such as Kansas and Iowa
The East, in states such as Virginia and Kentucky
Louisiana bayous first settled by French farmers
Alaska, where the land was first surveyed by satellite

why.correct: Metes and bounds describes land by distances and natural landmarks. It was the method of the eastern colonies, so their field patterns are irregular.
options: Kansas and Iowa were surveyed later with the township and range grid.
Right: metes and bounds was used in the original colonies and some states formed from them.
French settlement in Louisiana left long lots, panel 3.
Satellite surveying is not one of the three methods shown.

items.q: Which survey method does the passage describe?
options: Metes and bounds
Long lot
Township and range
Linear settlement

why.correct: The Land Ordinance set up the rectangular survey known as township and range.
options: Metes and bounds uses natural landmarks and irregular lines, not a planned grid of squares.
Long lots are narrow strips running back from a river, not squares.
Right: squares 6 miles on a side split into 36 one-square-mile sections is township and range.
Linear settlement is a pattern of houses along a line, not a survey method.

items.q: Using the passage, how many acres are in one township?

mistakes.why: A township is 6 miles on a side, so it holds 6 × 6 = 36 sections, not 6. Multiply 36 sections by 640 acres.
That is one section. A township has 36 sections of 640 acres each.

items.q: Based on the passage, what settlement pattern did this way of selling land most likely produce on farmland in states such as Iowa?
options: Dispersed farmhouses, each set on its own square of land
Clustered villages with fields spread around the village edge
Linear rows of houses along one long riverbank
No permanent settlement, because herders moved with the seasons

why.correct: The survey method shaped the settlement pattern: square parcels sold to single families produced dispersed settlement across the Midwest.
options: Right: families bought their own section or part of one and built on it, so houses spread out across the grid.
Selling land in separate squares to separate families led people to live on their own land, not in villages.
A row of houses along a river fits long lots, not the square grid.
The land was sold to farmers who settled on it.

items.q: In many villages in England, houses, a church and shops sit close together, and farmers walk out to fields around the village. What settlement pattern is this?
options: Dispersed
Clustered
Linear
Long lot

why.correct: Clustered settlement groups homes in a village and keeps farmland outside it.
options: Dispersed settlement scatters homes across the land, one on each farm.
Right: homes grouped together, with farmland around them, is clustered (nucleated) settlement.
Linear settlement lines homes along a road, river or shore.
Long lot is a survey method, not a settlement pattern.

items.q: In Egypt, most villages stretch along the Nile and the canals beside it, with houses in long lines. What best explains this linear pattern?
options: The government divided the land into a square grid of sections
Herders moved their homes with the seasons along the river
Villages were built for defense on hilltops away from the river
People settle near the water that makes farming possible in the desert

why.correct: A linear settlement follows a line on the land: here, the Nile and its canals in the desert.
options: A square grid fits township and range, which leads to dispersed farms, not lines.
Most Egyptian farmers in the Nile valley live in fixed homes, not moving herds.
Hilltop villages for defense would be clustered and away from the water.
Right: the river and canals bring water to crops, so homes line up along them.

items.q: Which is a common reason farm families choose to live in clustered villages instead of on their own scattered farms?
options: Sharing wells, defense, a market and a place of worship
Each family wants to live right beside the fields it farms
The land was sold in separate squares to single families
Farmers want the shortest walk from their house to their crops

why.correct: Clustering trades a longer walk to the fields for shared water, safety, services and community.
options: Right: living close together makes it easier to share services and protect one another.
Living beside your own fields leads to dispersed settlement.
Separate squares sold to families led to dispersed farms in the US Midwest.
In a clustered village farmers walk farther to their fields: that is a cost of clustering.

items.q: Which statements about rural settlement and survey methods are accurate? Select all that apply.
options: Township and range creates a grid of square fields and roads
Metes and bounds uses natural features such as streams and trees as boundaries
Long lots are found mainly in the dry grasslands of Mongolia
A dispersed pattern places homes together in one village
Linear settlement scatters farmhouses evenly across a grid

why.correct: Survey methods divide land; settlement patterns describe where homes sit. The method a place used often shaped its pattern.
options: Right: the grid is visible from the air over much of the US Midwest.
Right: that is why its fields have irregular shapes.
Long lots were laid out by French settlers along rivers in places such as Quebec and Louisiana.
Homes grouped in a village is clustered settlement.
Linear settlement lines homes along a road, river or shore.

items.q: From an airplane over Kansas you see roads in a grid about 1 mile apart. At what scale of analysis is this grid best described, and what made it?
options: Local: each farmer chose where to put the roads
Global: the same grid covers farmland around the world
Regional: a national survey law applied across many states
Local: river banks set the line of each road

why.correct: The grid repeats across the Midwest and West, a regional pattern produced by a national survey system.
options: Farmers did not choose the lines; the national survey did, the same way across many states.
Long lots in Quebec and metes and bounds in Virginia show the grid is not everywhere.
Right: the grid covers a whole region of the country, and it comes from the US township and range survey.
River banks shape long lots, not a grid of straight roads.

items.q: Why do farms in Virginia often have irregular shapes, while farms in Iowa are mostly squares?
options: Virginia has a desert climate that makes square fields hard to irrigate
Iowa farmers practice shifting cultivation and move their fields
Virginia was divided into long lots by French settlers along its rivers
They were surveyed at different times with different methods

why.correct: Survey methods leave a lasting mark. Colonial metes and bounds left irregular parcels in Virginia; the 1785 grid left squares across Iowa.
options: Virginia has a wet climate; the shapes come from how the land was first divided.
Iowa has mixed crop and livestock farming on fixed fields.
Long lots fit French settlement in Quebec and Louisiana, not Virginia.
Right: Virginia used metes and bounds in colonial times; Iowa was later surveyed by township and range.

items.q: A deed from 1790 in Kentucky marks a farm boundary at "the large oak by the creek." Which problem is most likely to arise from this metes and bounds description?
options: The farm is forced into a square exactly one mile on each side
The boundary becomes unclear when the tree dies or the creek moves
The farm has no access to water because it is far from the creek
Houses on the farm line up along a road in a linear pattern

why.correct: Metes and bounds relies on landmarks. When landmarks change, neighbors may disagree on where the line is: a known limit of the method.
options: A fixed square of one mile is a section in township and range, not metes and bounds.
Right: features that change or vanish make metes and bounds lines hard to find, which leads to disputes.
The deed puts the boundary at the creek, so the farm touches it.
The deed describes a boundary, not where houses stand.

items.q: Compared with families in a clustered village in India, farm families in dispersed settlement in Kansas are most likely to face which challenge?
options: Longer walks each morning from home to their fields
Less land for each family than in the village
Longer trips to schools, stores and neighbors
Boundaries that follow streams and trees

why.correct: Dispersed and clustered settlement trade off differently: dispersed homes are close to the fields but far from services; clustered homes are the reverse.
options: That is a cost of clustered settlement: villagers walk out to their fields.
Kansas farms are large; dispersed homes sit on big parcels.
Right: with each home on its own farm, services are spread far apart.
Kansas was surveyed by township and range, a grid.

items.q: Build an explanation of how a survey method shaped a settlement pattern in a named place.

why.correct: Name the place, the method and the effect with its link (so): long lots put every house on the river, a linear pattern.

specific.frame: In ___, land was divided by ___, so ___.
specific.model: In Quebec along the St. Lawrence River, land was divided by long lots, so farmhouses line up along the river in a linear pattern.

place.label: Place
options: Quebec along the St. Lawrence River
Kansas
a farming region

why.1: Kansas was surveyed with the township and range grid, not long lots.
why.2: Name a real place; a vague one earns no credit.

cause.label: Survey method
options: long lots
township and range

why.1: French settlers along the St. Lawrence used long lots, not the US grid.

effect.label: Effect
options: farmhouses line up along the river in a linear pattern
farmhouses cluster in one village on a hill

why.1: Each family built on its own river frontage, making a line, not a cluster.
